title: I Reported the Fake Handicap Placard at the Farmers-Market Lot

parts.text: I circled the market lot at 8:12 a.m. with an actual placard hanging from my mirror. A lifted truck sat in the last access space with a photocopy of a placard taped to the glass. I was forty-seven, cane in the passenger footwell. The photocopy still had a JPEG halo. I photographed the halo, the plate, and my own dated tag. Then I told the market manager, who said they do not do parking. At 8:18 a city traffic officer on coffee foot patrol asked why I was waving him toward a truck.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The officer is looking at a JPEG halo on the last access space.

social.video_title: Photocopy placard in the last access spot — Part 1/2
social.description: Real tag, cane, market manager declined. Coffee patrol arrived. Would you have kept circling?

parts.text: The officer ticketed the photocopy. The truck left in a sulk. I parked. I bought peaches. The manager decided they do parking when cities do. JPEG is not a disability. My cane hit the pavement like a period. The lot had a space again. I do not clap for tickets. I clap for peaches that made it into a tote from a legal spot.

social.video_title: The photocopy got a real ticket — Part 2/2
social.description: Truck sulk, peaches, manager converted. Was a halo a placard?
